products.name: AFSV VRC Training Tee
products.shot: Product shot — folded training tee, front
products.blurb: Breathable training layer in district colours.
products.desc: The standard training layer for AFSV VRC programs, in a breathable knit that holds its shape through repeat washing.
products.long: Worn across youth, adult and adaptive program streams. Cut for movement rather than fit-to-size fashion sizing, with flat seams at the shoulder to reduce rub under bibs and vests.

products.name: Performance Hoodie
products.shot: Product shot — hoodie on hanger, front
products.desc: Mid-weight hooded layer for warmups, travel and sideline wear, with a brushed inner face.
products.long: Built as the travel layer for program squads. Sized to layer over a training tee without restricting the shoulder.

products.name: Sensory-Friendly Warmup Jacket
products.shot: Product shot — warmup jacket, tag-free interior
products.desc: Warmup jacket designed with sensory sensitivity in mind: no interior tags, reduced seams and a fabric chosen for low rustle.
products.long: Developed with the Neurodiversity Access & Opportunity program. Fastenings are magnetic rather than zip-toothed, and all labelling is heat-transferred onto the outer face.
specs: Seam count reduced at collar and cuff

products.name: Noise-Reducing Ear Defenders
products.shot: Product shot — folded ear defenders, side
products.desc: Folding ear defenders for use in loud training halls, arenas and event venues.
products.long: Stocked at the facility desk for loan as well as sale. Sized for youth and adult heads with an adjustable band.

products.name: Court Grip Trainer
products.shot: Product shot — grip trainer on court floor
products.desc: Footwork trainer for change-of-direction and deceleration work on indoor courts.
products.long: Used in development-stream sessions. Non-marking base, suitable for sprung and coated hardwood.

products.name: Weighted Skills Ball 2 kg
products.desc: Textured 2 kg ball for throwing, catching and core progressions.
products.long: Standard kit item across strength and conditioning progressions. Sand-filled, so it does not roll away when set down mid-drill.

products.name: Coach Clipboard Set
products.shot: Product shot — clipboard with session sheets
products.desc: Coaching clipboard with dry-wipe court face and a pad of AFSV VRC session sheets.
products.long: Issued to program coaches. Session sheet layout matches the reporting fields used for participation records.

products.name: Focus & Fuel Recovery Mix
products.desc: Post-session recovery mix, unflavoured or citrus, made in Ontario.
products.long: Stocked for adult program participants. Ingredient and allergen labelling is supplied by the vendor and must be verified before public sale.

products.name: Team Water Bottle 1 L
products.desc: One-litre insulated bottle with a space for squad and participant marking.
products.long: Issued with membership welcome packs and sold individually. Wide mouth for ice and cleaning.

products.name: Youth Skills Camp Day Pass
products.shot: Product shot / booking card — camp day pass
products.desc: Single-day admission to a youth skills camp session, redeemable against a scheduled date.
products.long: Sold as a simple product in this preview. On the live site this becomes a bookable product tied to the facility calendar, and access-fund support is applied at the point of booking.
specs: Access fund support applied at booking

ship.label: Pickup at Whitby Smart Sports Village
ship.note: Available once the site is operational.

/programs.h1: Develop the Athlete. Strengthen the Whole Person.
/programs.lead: AFSV VRC is developing inclusive pathways intended to support participation, skill development, performance, confidence and opportunity.
/programs.alt: A coach crouching to talk with two teenage athletes during a session in an indoor fieldhouse, other participants of mixed ages and abilities training behind them, one using a sport wheelchair.
/programs.note: Program details coming soon. Schedules, coaching assignments, prices and capacity are not confirmed and are not published on this page.
/programs.listLead: Ten categories planned for the first program cycle. Each will carry its own status label until confirmed.

blocks.title: Structured records
blocks.body: Approved title, status, age group, ability level, format, schedule, location, capacity, prerequisites, accessibility, coach or provider, price, media and registration route.

blocks.title: Status labels
blocks.body: Every program carries a visible status. Until it is approved the record shows “Program details coming soon” and collects interest only.

blocks.title: Adaptive pathway
blocks.body: Adaptive and sensory-friendly sport is a named category in its own right, not an accommodation applied to another program.

blocks.title: Registration later
blocks.body: Registration and payment stay switched off until inventory, schedules, pricing, waivers and refund terms are approved.

form.title: Register program interest.
form.lead: Tell us who the participant is and what they are interested in. We collect only what is needed for a first conversation.
form.note: Do not include diagnoses or medical records. Accessibility needs are optional and free-text.

fields.ph: Anything that would help us plan a session well

/programs.ctaHead: Coaches and providers register through a separate route.

/education.h1: Learning That Builds Confidence and Capability
/education.lead: AFSV VRC is developing academic support intended to help young people develop academically as well as physically and socially.
/education.alt: Two teenagers working at a table with notebooks and a laptop in a study space beside a training hall, an adult tutor leaning in to help.
/education.note: No tutoring service, diagnostic assessment, regulated support, named provider, curriculum approval or school partnership is live. Nothing here should be read as an available service.
/education.listLead: Twelve areas of planned academic support.
/education.blocksTitle: How support is intended to work.

blocks.title: Alongside training
blocks.body: Study time sits inside the program schedule rather than competing with it, so participants are not choosing between the two.

blocks.title: Shared reporting
blocks.body: Where a school partnership is in place, coaches and educators work from the same progress information — with consent.

blocks.title: No clinical claims
blocks.body: Academic coaching is not assessment, diagnosis or regulated therapeutic support, and is never described as such.

blocks.title: Data minimisation
blocks.body: Public forms ask for the least information needed. Anything sensitive moves to an approved secure process later.

/education.list2Lead: Five routes, kept separate so families and institutions are not funnelled into one inbox.

form.title: Register learning interest.
form.lead: For families, learners, educators and institutions. Tell us which route applies.
form.note: We do not ask for diagnoses, assessments or medical records. Accommodation requests are optional.

fields.ph: Optional — anything that would help us respond well

/education.ctaHead: Schools, colleges and tutors have their own route.

/life-skills.lead: Life-skills programming is intended to prepare participants for independence, leadership, careers and entrepreneurship.
/life-skills.alt: A small-group life skills workshop: five young adults around a table in a bright community room with a facilitator standing and explaining.

ctas.label: Become a Mentor or Delivery Partner

/life-skills.note: All facilitators, curricula, safeguarding requirements, outcomes, dates and fees remain pending approval. No sessions are scheduled and none should be presented as available.
/life-skills.listLead: Thirteen themes, delivered in short blocks rather than as a single course.

blocks.title: Workshops
blocks.body: Short facilitated sessions on a single theme, sized to fit inside an existing program block. Subject to approved facilitators and schedules.

blocks.title: Mentoring
blocks.body: One-to-one and small-group mentoring, with mentors screened before any participant contact.

blocks.title: Integrated modules
blocks.body: Themes built into athlete-development sessions so the learning is not separated from the training.

blocks.title: Family resources
blocks.body: Material families can use at home, written in plain language.

blocks.title: Partner-led learning
blocks.body: Sessions delivered by employer, education and community partners under the same safeguarding requirements.

form.title: Register interest.
form.lead: For participants, families, and anyone offering to mentor or deliver.
form.note: Safeguarding screening applies to every mentor and delivery partner before contact with participants.

/life-skills.ctaHead: Sponsors fund whole blocks of life-skills programming.

/technology-media.h1: New Pathways to Create, Compete and Build
/technology-media.lead: Not every participant connects with traditional sport. These pathways are intended to support social connection, skills, confidence, storytelling and career exploration.
/technology-media.alt: A broadcast production desk with a mixing console in the foreground and a row of competition stations behind, a young adult in headphones working at the desk.
/technology-media.note: No equipment, studio, event, platform, partner technology or instruction is operational. Media participation requires consent, and safeguarding requirements apply to participants under 18.
/technology-media.listLead: Eleven pathways, each with its own progression and supervision requirements.

blocks.title: Competition and production space
blocks.body: A room that can run a tournament and produce the coverage of it. Subject to final design and procurement.

blocks.title: Broadcast booth
blocks.body: Commentary and live coverage position for AFSV VRC programs. Conceptual — not built.

blocks.title: Podcast studio
blocks.body: Recording space for participant and community storytelling. Conceptual — not built.

blocks.title: Learning labs
blocks.body: Coding, STEM and AI education rooms. Equipment specification is not finalised.

form.title: Register program interest.
form.lead: Separate routes for participants, technology partners and media collaboration.
form.note: Media and broadcast participation requires documented consent. For participants under 18, guardian consent and safeguarding checks apply before any recording.

/technology-media.ctaHead: Technology and media partners shape these pathways.

/gaisb-ai.h1: Advancing Responsible AI Education and Workforce Readiness
/gaisb-ai.lead: Through its strategic relationship with the Global AI Standards Body, AFSV VRC is advancing AI education, certification, workforce readiness and responsible innovation across sport, education and community development in Canada and the Caribbean.
/gaisb-ai.alt: Three adult learners working at a long desk with large displays showing abstract data visualisations, while an instructor explains a concept in a modern technology education studio.
/gaisb-ai.note: This is a strategic relationship with the Global AI Standards Body. No accreditation, exclusivity or course availability is claimed beyond approved language, and no GAISB logo or brand mark is published pending written permission. Programs, territories, certifications, fees and dates appear only once contractually approved.
/gaisb-ai.listLead: Eight pathways within the confirmed scope of the relationship.
/gaisb-ai.blocksTitle: AI supports the pillars. It does not replace them.

blocks.title: Athlete development
blocks.body: Analysis and planning tools support coaching decisions. The coach makes the decision.

blocks.title: Inclusive learning
blocks.body: Assistive and adaptive tools widen access to material. They do not substitute for a teacher or a support worker.

blocks.title: Neurodivergent support
blocks.body: Tools chosen for accessibility and predictability, reviewed with the people who use them.

blocks.title: Operations
blocks.body: Scheduling, reporting and administration, so staff time goes to participants rather than paperwork.

blocks.title: Media and career preparation
blocks.body: Production and career-readiness skills that reflect how the work is actually done now.

form.title: Certification, education and enterprise inquiries.
form.lead: Tell us which pathway applies and we will route your inquiry to the right team.
form.note: No certification, fee, territory or date is confirmed by this form. Responses describe approved scope only.

fields.ph: What you are trying to achieve

/gaisb-ai.ctaHead: Enterprise and education partners engage separately.

/neurodiversity.lead: AFSV VRC is developing an inclusive ecosystem intended to expand access to sport, education, developmental support, life skills, technology and employment for neurodivergent people. Through qualified professionals, community organizations, businesses, sponsors and employers, the program intends to reduce financial and accessibility barriers.
/neurodiversity.alt: Five adults of varied backgrounds in a loose circle doing a low-intensity warm-up led by a coach in a calm indoor hall; one participant wears noise-reducing earmuffs and another moves at their own pace, clearly included.
/neurodiversity.note: AFSV VRC does not provide clinical diagnosis, assessment or therapeutic treatment. Regulated services are delivered only by qualified professionals who are reviewed separately, and the public form does not ask for diagnoses or medical records.
/neurodiversity.listLead: Written as the community describes itself. Identity-first and person-first preferences are both respected.

blocks.title: Individuals
blocks.body: Register interest in programs and support, and hear back from a named contact rather than a general inbox.

blocks.title: Families and carers
blocks.body: Plain-language information, a vetted provider directory, and help working out what is available.

blocks.title: Professionals and providers
blocks.body: Apply to join the Service Provider Network, subject to qualification, insurance and safeguarding review.

blocks.title: Businesses and employers
blocks.body: Join Business for Inclusion as a funding, service, employment, commercial or accessibility partner.

/neurodiversity.list2Lead: Eight pathways, each qualified until the service behind it is approved.

form.title: Get support or register interest.
form.lead: An initial inquiry only. A named contact will respond by your preferred method.
form.note: We do not ask for a diagnosis or medical records. Accommodation information is optional and free-text, and anything sensitive moves to an approved secure process later.

fields.ph: Optional — anything that would help us communicate well with you

/neurodiversity.ctaHead: Cost should not decide who takes part.

/business-for-inclusion.h1: Your Business Can Help Remove Barriers
/business-for-inclusion.lead: AFSV VRC is developing a network of businesses committed to creating opportunities for neurodivergent individuals and families.
/business-for-inclusion.alt: A mentor and a younger colleague working together at a desk in an inclusive modern office, with colleagues at nearby desks — one wearing over-ear headphones, one at a standing desk in a quieter corner.
/business-for-inclusion.note: Sponsorship values and packages are administrator-configurable and are not published. Submissions feed an internal review workflow and are never auto-published.
/business-for-inclusion.listLead: Seven ways a business can take part.

blocks.title: Employer readiness
blocks.body: A review of recruitment practice, interview format and workplace environment before any candidate is introduced.

blocks.title: Role design
blocks.body: Roles written around the work that needs doing and the strengths of the candidate, not a generic job description.

blocks.title: Configurable contribution
blocks.body: Values and packages are set by an administrator, so nothing is hardcoded and nothing is published before approval.

blocks.title: Reviewed, not listed
blocks.body: A submission starts a review. It does not create a public listing, a logo placement or an announced partnership.

/business-for-inclusion.list2Lead: Sponsorship framed around what it changes for a participant.

form.title: Business and employer inquiries.
form.lead: One form, routed by pathway. Investor and sponsorship inquiries reach different teams.
form.note: No sponsorship value is agreed by this form, and no partnership is published without written approval.

/business-for-inclusion.ctaHead: Sponsorship values are set per agreement, never published in advance.

/service-provider-network.h1: Become an AFSV VRC Service Provider
/service-provider-network.lead: AFSV VRC intends to build a qualified network supporting sport, learning, development, wellbeing and inclusion.
/service-provider-network.alt: Two professionals in smart casual clothing seated across a low table in a calm, non-clinical consulting room, reviewing printed materials and a tablet together.
/service-provider-network.note: Submission does not approve or publicly list a provider. All providers remain subject to qualification, licence and registration, insurance, safeguarding, privacy, capacity and agreement reviews.
/service-provider-network.listLead: Ten categories under consideration. A category being listed does not mean a provider is available.

blocks.title: Qualification and registration
blocks.body: Regulated professions must evidence current licence or registration. Those fields are conditional and only appear where they apply.

blocks.title: Insurance and safeguarding
blocks.body: Professional indemnity, screening and safeguarding arrangements are checked before any participant contact.

blocks.title: Capacity and coverage
blocks.body: Age groups, specialisation, geography and delivery mode, so referrals are only made where a provider can genuinely take them.

blocks.title: Agreement and listing
blocks.body: Listing follows a signed agreement. Until then a submission sits in a review queue with an auditable status.

form.title: Register provider interest.
form.lead: This is an application to be reviewed, not a listing request.
form.note: Licence and registration fields are conditional on regulated profession. Do not attach client records or identifying participant information.

fields.ph: Anything else the review should consider

/service-provider-network.ctaHead: Families use the network. Providers apply to join it.

/neurodiversity-access-fund.lead: AFSV VRC intends to develop a funding mechanism helping eligible individuals and families access selected programs and services regardless of financial circumstances.
/neurodiversity-access-fund.alt: A quiet still-life on a long charcoal table: trainers, a notebook and pen, a tablet, a water bottle, a folded towel and keys, evenly spaced in soft side light — everyday things that access makes possible.
/neurodiversity-access-fund.note: AFSV VRC is not a charity. No donation receipt, tax deductibility, eligibility, funding availability or free service is promised. Contribution and payment functionality remains disabled until legal structure, accounting, privacy, eligibility and fund-administration rules are approved. The form below is an expression of interest, not a donation.
/neurodiversity-access-fund.listLead: Ten possible sources. None is confirmed, and none implies charitable status.
/neurodiversity-access-fund.blocksTitle: How the mechanism is intended to work.

blocks.title: Configurable outcomes
blocks.body: Sponsored outcomes and their values are administrator-configurable. Nothing is hardcoded and nothing is published before approval.

blocks.title: No payment route
blocks.body: There is no Donate button and no payment processing anywhere on this page. Expressions of interest are handled by people, not a gateway.

blocks.title: Eligibility later
blocks.body: Eligibility thresholds, award schedules and application windows follow legal, accounting and privacy sign-off.

blocks.title: Reported in aggregate
blocks.body: Awards are recorded for governance and reported in aggregate. No identifying participant information is published.

/neurodiversity-access-fund.list2Lead: Framed by what the funding changes, not by a price.

form.title: Express funding interest.
form.lead: For sponsors, businesses and contributors. This starts a conversation — it does not transfer any funds.
form.note: This is an expression of interest, not a donation. No receipt, deductibility or funding commitment follows from it.

fields.ph: What you would like to support

/neurodiversity-access-fund.ctaHead: Businesses fund access through Business for Inclusion.

leadership.name: Martin Lashley
bio: Martin Lashley is the Founder, Chairman, and Interim Chief Executive Officer of Athletes & Fans Sports Village Holding Company Limited (AFSVHCL), a Canadian-based sports infrastructure and youth development company building an integrated ecosystem that combines elite sport, education support, sports science, esports, and community engagement.
leadership.alt: Martin Lashley standing on the turf inside an indoor sports dome.

leadership.name: Natalie Sutherland-Lashley
bio: Natalie Sutherland-Lashley serves as Co-Chairperson and Corporate Secretary of Athletes & Fans Sports Village Holding Company Limited (AFSVHCL), where she plays a critical role in the governance, strategic development, and international positioning of the organization.

With a strong background in business administration, organizational leadership, and corporate governance, Natalie helps guide the operational structure and long-term strategy behind the Athletes & Fans Sports Village vision. Her work supports the company's mission of building a next-generation global sports ecosystem that integrates elite athletic development, education, wellness, esports, and community inclusion.

As Co-Chairperson, Natalie works closely with the executive leadership team to ensure that AFSVHCL maintains the highest standards of corporate accountability, transparency, and stakeholder engagement. She is responsible for coordinating board governance, overseeing corporate documentation, and helping manage the strategic relationships that underpin the company's expansion across Canada, the Caribbean, and the broader international sports community.

Natalie is also a passionate advocate for the project's social impact mission, particularly its commitment to creating opportunities for youth and families while integrating education and support programs for neurodivergent children and individuals with learning differences.

Through her work with AFSVHCL, Natalie continues to contribute to the development of a transformational sports and education platform designed to inspire the next generation of athletes, innovators, and community leaders.

leadership.name: Michelle Lashley
bio: Michelle Lashley serves as the Chief Operating Officer of Athletes & Fans Sports Village Holding Company Limited (AFSVHCL), where she oversees the operational execution of the company's global sports, education, and community development initiatives.

With extensive experience in organizational management, program development, and strategic implementation, Michelle plays a pivotal role in transforming the Athletes & Fans Sports Village vision into a fully operational ecosystem. She leads the coordination of internal operations, strategic partnerships, and program delivery across the company's expanding initiatives in Canada, the Caribbean, and the United States.

As COO, Michelle is responsible for ensuring that the organization's core pillars — elite athletic development, education, wellness, esports innovation, and community inclusion — are executed efficiently and sustainably. She works closely with the executive leadership team to implement operational systems, manage key stakeholder relationships, and ensure the successful rollout of major projects including the Whitby Smart Sports Village pilot in Ontario and related international initiatives.

Michelle is also the Founder of MLMSR Mentorship LLC, an education and mentorship organization that supports the Athletes & Fans Sports Village platform through academic programming, mentorship initiatives, and specialized education support for neurodivergent youth, including individuals on the autism spectrum and those with ADHD and dyslexia.
Through her role at AFSVHCL, Michelle continues to help shape a transformative platform designed to empower athletes, support families, and build sustainable sports communities around the world.
leadership.quote: “We operate with purpose, execute with excellence, and serve with heart to create opportunities that change lives and strengthen communities.”

leadership.name: Vinai Charran
leadership.role: Chief Investor, AFSVHCL · CEO, Charran's Group of Companies
bio: Vinai Charran serves as Chief Investor for Athletes & Fans Sports Village Holding Company Limited (AFSVHCL) and plays a central role in supporting the organization's strategic growth and capital development initiatives.

A successful entrepreneur and international businessman, Vinai brings extensive experience in investment strategy, business development, and global commercial operations. His leadership and financial support help advance the Athletes & Fans Sports Village vision of building a next-generation global sports, education, and community development ecosystem.

Vinai is the CEO of Charran's Group of Companies, a diversified business enterprise with operations spanning retail, education, publishing, and international trade. Through decades of entrepreneurial leadership, he has established a reputation for identifying innovative opportunities and building sustainable business platforms that deliver long-term value.

Within AFSVHCL, Vinai provides strategic investment leadership and supports the development of major initiatives, including the Whitby Smart Sports Village pilot project in Ontario, Canada, which will serve as the foundation for a broader national and international rollout of integrated sports, education, and community infrastructure.

Through his partnership with AFSVHCL, Vinai continues to help drive the development of a globally scalable sports and education platform designed to inspire athletes, empower communities, and foster innovation in youth development worldwide.

focus.d: Driving capital growth and long-term value creation for AFSVHCL.
Building international partnerships and expanding business opportunities.
Investing in initiatives that empower youth, promote education, and strengthen communities.
Supporting innovative, scalable projects with a focus on long-term sustainability and global impact.

leadership.quote: “I believe in the power of sports and education to transform lives and build stronger communities. My investment in AFSVHCL is an investment in our youth and in a better future for generations to come.”
leadership.quoteBy: — Vinai Charran, CEO, Charran's Group of Companies

events.summary: AI is joining the workforce. Money is going digital. AI agents now connect the two. Three days in Port of Spain for the people shaping what comes next: CEOs and executives, governments and regulators, financial professionals, investors and builders.
